newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-SELES TURNS BLIND EYE TO PARISIAN ATTRACTIONS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES TURNS BLIND EYE TO PARISIAN ATTRACTIONS.

text.p: The familiar delights of Paris are failing to distract Monica Seles from the job of rebuilding her previously impregnable grand slam reputation at Roland Garros.

Seles used to love exploring the French capital as a teenager in the days when she was practically a Parisian attraction in her own right by virtue of her three successive titles between 1990 and 1992.
This year, though, she has been conspicuous by her absence from the city's restaurants and cafes and the 23-year-old confirms she has barely ventured out during the tournament's opening week.
"For the first five days I stayed in my hotel and had room service," revealed Seles, whose career prizemoney earnings of over nine million dollars have long given her the freedom to dine a la carte.
"Last night a friend of mine arrived and we went to the Louvre and had dinner, but it's harder now because I sometimes feel guilty doing some things. I'm trying to keep it real low-key right now."

How much her life outside tennis is still affected by the Hamburg stabbing in April 1993 which cost her two years of here career remains a matter for conjecture, but there are signs that Seles is gradually rediscovering some of her old authority on the court.

Ironically, a broken finger gave her a chance to rest her long-term shoulder problem earlier this year and, although her serve is still suspect, most other areas of her game looked in good order during a 6-0 6-1 mauling of France's Nathalie Tauziat on centre court on Saturday.

So one-sided did the match become that Tauziat threw her arms aloft in mock triumph after breaking Seles in the fifth game of the second set to register her solitary game and the entire contest lasted just 51 minutes.

"I think Nathalie made more unforced errors than she usually does," said Seles diplomatically. "I was passing well but my serve was very bad. Against the good players I need to have it all together, not just one or two parts of my game. I have to stay more focussed than I have been in the past few months.
Seles' only defeat in Paris since her first visit in 1989 when she reached the semifinals was a quarter-final loss to Jana Novotna in the quarter-finals last year.
She can now look ahead to a last 16 meeting with France's Mary Pierce, an opponent who may test her new reliance on defence as a method of achieving victory.
"I played a very weird match against Mary Pierce in Rome so hopefully i can improve on that," Seles said.
"She hits the ball very hard, so it will be very fast tennis. I can't play defensivly against Mary...she'll just blow me off the court."
